thread:
Anjali: paging — we're seeing a p99 / streaming-tail spike in eu-central1 starting ~15:03 UTC, lots of stalled streams and TLS handshake timeouts. customer-facing error rate up.

incident-bot: HIGH severity incident opened and paged oncall Anjali (eu). Alert: streaming_tail_p99 > 6s for 5m, tls_handshake_retries spike, nat-egress-error-rate > 0.8%.

Kevin: grabbing context. what's the scope? single AZ or cross-zone?

Anjali: looks cross-AZ. metric heatmap shows increased retransmits from instances in az-a/az-b toward nat-gw-eu-01. p95 ~1.1s, p99 ~6.8s on streaming tails.

Maria: I can see packet loss counters bumping on nat-gw-eu-01, and conntrack entries climbing fast. `conntrack -S` showing sustained growth. Could be ephemeral port churn or backing NAT process.

Sam: Support says 7 paying customers reported stalled streaming sessions, one on dedicated capacity. We should start mitigation and customer updates.

Anjali: mitigation plan: 1) divert new egress to nat-gw-eu-02, 2) bump conntrack limits on nat-gw-eu-01 as short-term, 3) enable TCP keepalive tweaks if needed, 4) monitor streaming tail and TLS retry metrics.

Kevin: I'll run the route update for canary traffic to nat-gw-eu-02 for 10% first.

Maria: On nat-gw-eu-01: `sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=524288` and `sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range=\"1024 65535\"` to give temporary headroom. Also increasing `nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established` to avoid churn.

Anjali: please post the exact commands you run. don't change anything irreversible.

Maria: running now.

Maria: command log:

```
sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=524288
sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range=\"1024 65535\"
sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established=86400
```

Maria: conntrack count stabilized briefly but still trending up — looks like we're absorbing more connections but underlying retransmits persist.

Kevin: deploying route change: updating route table rt-eu-streams -> target nat-gw-eu-02 for weight=10%. will monitor.

incident-bot: Route-change event: rt-eu-streams weight update to nat-gw-eu-02=10% by Kevin.

Sam: started customer notify: short message that we're investigating egress path issues affecting streaming quality in eu, ETA 30m for mitigation.

Anjali: good. also snapshot tcpdump on nat-gw-eu-01 for TLS handshake failures: `sudo tcpdump -i eth0 'tcp[tcpflags] & (tcp-syn|tcp-ack) != 0' -w /tmp/handshake.pcap`

Kevin: can confirm observation — when traffic shifts to nat-gw-eu-02 p99 drops to ~2.2s for the canary, streaming stalls reduce. nat-gw-eu-01 still showing high retransmits.

Maria: digging deeper: kernel logs on nat-gw-eu-01 show `NETDEV WATCHDOG` and some NIC driver resets in the last hour. Could be hardware flapping under load.

Sam: do we have spare capacity to move all traffic to nat-gw-eu-02 while we investigate? Any cross-AZ network constraints?

Anjali: we can increase to 50% now, but watch latency to customers in az-c. if no regression push to 100%.

Kevin: increasing to 50% now.

incident-bot: Route-change event: rt-eu-streams weight update to nat-gw-eu-02=50% by Kevin.

Kevin: after 50% shift p99 across region dropped from 6.8s -> 2.4s, TLS handshake retries back to baseline. Customer error reports decreased.

Maria: propose we failover active flows off nat-gw-eu-01 by updating the NAT attachment and cordoning that instance for deeper inspection. If it's NIC hardware, we should replace it.

Anjali: agree. cordon and replace. Sam, coordinate with Support to escalate impacted customers for a follow-up.

Support: acknowledged — informing affected customers that we've rerouted traffic and are replacing faulty gateway; offering monitoring updates and post-incident follow-up.

Sam: adding quick customer note to accounts slack and sending targeted messages with incident id.

Anjali: handoff: I'm going offline for a short break, handing incident lead to Kevin. Kevin — keep an eye on p99 and streaming tail for the next 45m and coordinate gateway replacement.

Kevin: taking lead. Will start cordon of nat-gw-eu-01: `cloudctl instances cordon nat-gw-eu-01 --drain` then create replacement instance and reattach routes.

Maria: I'll collect `dmesg` and `ethtool -S` output and upload to the incident artifacts bucket for postmortem.

Kevin: cordon started. show logs:

```
$ cloudctl instances cordon nat-gw-eu-01 --drain
Cordoning nat-gw-eu-01... connections draining (ETA ~2m)
Updating route weights... succeeded
```

Kevin: spun up nat-gw-eu-03 and shifted remaining traffic over. p99 now steady at 1.8s region-wide.

incident-bot: Incident update: mitigation in progress, traffic shifted away from nat-gw-eu-01; p99 streaming_tail reduced to 1.8s.

Anjali: thanks team. Once replacement is validated file a postmortem and include timelines, root cause hypothesis (NIC flapping + conntrack exhaustion), and customer impact summary.

Sam: creating incident doc and will notify PM/Trust teams.

Kevin: leaving nat-gw-eu-01 offline for hardware investigation. Will re-run soak tests on replacement before reintroducing.

Maria: uploaded diagnostics: /artifacts/incidents/2419990000/{dmesg,ethtool,conntrack-snap.txt,pcap}.

Support: customers updated; one enterprise customer requested a dedicated post-incident call — scheduling.

Anjali: incident severity will remain P1 until final verification and customer confirmations. I'll check back in 2 hours for handoff if needed.

Kevin: noted. continuing monitoring.

incident-bot: Incident P1 still open — assignee: Kevin.

Anjali: thanks all — nice coordinated work. :thumbsup:
